source.title: Negative arousal amplifies the effects of saliency in short-term memory.

confidence_rationale: A clean randomized-controlled behavioural demonstration that arousal is a selective (saliency-amplifying) modulator, not a uniform one: high-salience recall rises while low-salience recall does not change. This directly evidences the non-scalar functional form MECH-074b needs. Confidence held at 0.6 because the paradigm is short-term memory for letter arrays under pre-exposed arousing sounds -- attention/STM, not hippocampal long-term retrieval -- so transfer risk to MECH-074b's retrieval-weight-on-stored-traces mechanism is substantial.
failure_signatures: The selectivity is demonstrated in SHORT-TERM memory / attentional report of letter arrays, not in long-term declarative retrieval; it does not show a weight applied to consolidated hippocampal traces, and cannot speak to MECH-074b's trace-age growth claim.

Low-salience recall was unchanged (not impaired) on arousing trials -- so this experiment shows selective enhancement but not the absolute peripheral suppression seen in lesion data, leaving the additive-vs-competitive form question open.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Negative emotional arousal increases the selectivity of attention: on arousing trials recall of high-salience letters increased while recall of low-salience letters did not, providing evidence for arousal-biased competition (arousal enhances representations that have priority).
mapping.ree_translation: This is the empirical leg under MECH-074b's vector-not-scalar constraint: arousal amplifies the already-privileged (high-salience/central) items specifically, rather than lifting all items equally. It operationalises the per-trace weight w_i as a saliency-dependent multiplier -- high tag -> larger weight, low tag -> baseline -- exactly the shape MECH-074b posits.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Modality and timescale mismatch: this is visual short-term memory for letter arrays under fear-conditioned auditory arousal, measured seconds after presentation. MECH-074b concerns long-term hippocampal retrieval with a weight that grows over minutes-to-a-week. The direction of selectivity transfers; the retrieval-time and long-timescale claims do not.
mapping.source_context: Human behavioural RCT; participants heard negative-arousing vs neutral sounds before briefly viewing letter arrays with salience manipulated via visual contrast; partial-report recall.

confidence_components.notes: Solid controlled experiment (RCT design) -> source_quality 0.72. Mapping fidelity moderate: correct direction of selectivity, wrong memory system/timescale. Transfer risk high (0.5): STM/attention -> hippocampal LTM retrieval is a real leap.
